account: There is unusually coordinated activity around bread and supplies today. The secretary reports twenty-four loaves delivered to the town hall, and saw building materials handed over in an exchange involving the baker and builder. The baker has now confirmed to the secretary that builder, freight and innkeeper coordinated the hall deliveries, trading building supplies for grain. Neither the baker nor secretary has established who originally requested them or their purpose. Earlier I heard that the baker carried a sack of bread at the inn. This evening I personally saw my neighbour outside town hall carrying a sack of bread, although I do not know its destination. At tea the neighbour said they had met the innkeeper, builder, freight, baker and secretary this morning and offered help baking. A lantern was also installed in the hall today. Most notably, the innkeeper requested a meeting with me tomorrow at eighteen hundred in the great hall, specifically asking me not to arrive early and giving no purpose. Taken together, I suspect preparations for a communal gathering, perhaps a surprise celebration for me, rather than merely routine trade. That remains conjecture; I have no evidence of wrongdoing. The missing accounts are a separate unresolved matter: the treasury contains 128 emeralds, counted untouched, but no receipts or payment ledgers have been located. The secretary has authorized no new bread purchase. I should keep tomorrow's appointments, including the innkeeper's meeting at the agreed time, and avoid treating speculation as fact.
